topics.label: Welcome and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and outlines that the lecture will focus on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Principles of innate immune recognition: PAMPs, DAMPs, and PRRs
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system detects infection and cellular damage using conserved molecular patterns and strategically localized germline-encoded receptors.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptor systems, signaling, and inflammasomes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore specific pattern recognition receptor families, their intracellular signaling pathways, and the assembly of inflammasomes that activate inflammatory cytokines.

topics.label: Sentinel cell activation and leukocyte recruitment to inflamed tissue
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how activated sentinel cells stimulate the vascular endothelium to orchestrate leukocyte rolling, extravasation, and chemokine-directed migration into infected tissues.

topics.label: Lymphatic drainage and antigen transport to lymph nodes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes how sentinel dendritic cells and interstitial fluid drain through the lymphatic system to prime adaptive immune cells within lymph nodes.

topics.label: Pathology of excessive systemic inflammation and septic shock
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the dangerous clinical consequences when uncontrolled, widespread cytokine release induces systemic vasodilation and septic shock.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the passive and active mechanisms that extinguish acute inflammation, rebuild damaged tissue, and establish long-term containment structures such as granulomas.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the presentation and announces the topic of the next lecture.
